title: Python Database CRUD with SQLAlchemy ORM
description: Build a menu-driven CLI application using SQLAlchemy ORM with Student, Course, and Enrollment models
objective: Students will build a complete command-line application that performs CRUD operations on a SQLite database using SQLAlchemy ORM, with proper model relationships and a user-friendly menu interface

steps.title: Set Up Python Project and Install Dependencies
steps.instructions:
Create a new project folder and set up the environment:

```bash
mkdir techpath_crud
cd techpath_crud
python -m venv venv

# Activate virtual environment
# Windows:
venv\Scripts\activate
# Mac/Linux:
# source venv/bin/activate

# Install SQLAlchemy
pip install sqlalchemy
```

Create a file called `models.py` with the database setup:

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, sessionmaker

# Database URL (SQLite file in current directory)
DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///techpath.db"

# Create engine
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, echo=False)

# Base class for all models
Base = declarative_base()

# Session factory
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

def get_session():
    """Create and return a new database session."""
    return Session()

def init_db():
    """Create all tables in the database."""
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    print("Database initialized successfully!")
```

Create a file called `app.py` with a basic test:

```python
from models import init_db, get_session

def main():
    init_db()
    session = get_session()
    print("TechPath Institute - Student Management System")
    print("Database connected!")
    session.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run it: `python app.py`

**Verify:** You should see "Database initialized successfully!" and a `techpath.db` file should appear in your folder.

steps.title: Define SQLAlchemy Models with Relationships
steps.instructions:
Update `models.py` to add the three models. Add these imports and classes after the existing code:

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Float, Boolean, Date, DateTime, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from datetime import datetime, date


class Course(Base):
    __tablename__ = "courses"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    name = Column(String(100), unique=True, nullable=False)
    duration_months = Column(Integer, nullable=False)
    fee = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    # One course has many enrollments
    enrollments = relationship("Enrollment", back_populates="course", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Course(id={self.id}, name='{self.name}', fee={self.fee})"


class Student(Base):
    __tablename__ = "students"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    name = Column(String(100), nullable=False)
    email = Column(String(150), unique=True, nullable=False)
    phone = Column(String(15))
    city = Column(String(50), default="Bhopal")
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    enrolled_date = Column(Date, default=date.today)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    # One student has many enrollments
    enrollments = relationship("Enrollment", back_populates="student", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Student(id={self.id}, name='{self.name}', city='{self.city}')"


class Enrollment(Base):
    __tablename__ = "enrollments"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    student_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("students.id"), nullable=False)
    course_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("courses.id"), nullable=False)
    enrolled_date = Column(Date, default=date.today)
    status = Column(String(20), default="active")
    grade = Column(String(2))

    student = relationship("Student", back_populates="enrollments")
    course = relationship("Course", back_populates="enrollments")

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Enrollment(student_id={self.student_id}, course_id={self.course_id}, status='{self.status}')"
```

Delete the old `techpath.db` file and run `python app.py` again.

**Verify:** The database should now have 3 tables. You can check with DB Browser for SQLite (https://sqlitebrowser.org/) or by adding this to app.py:
```python
from sqlalchemy import inspect
inspector = inspect(engine)
print("Tables:", inspector.get_table_names())
```

Should print: `Tables: ['courses', 'enrollments', 'students']`

steps.title: Create CRUD Functions (Create and Read)
steps.instructions:
Create a new file called `crud.py` with create and read functions:

```python
from models import get_session, Course, Student, Enrollment
from sqlalchemy.orm import joinedload
from sqlalchemy import func


def seed_data():
    """Insert sample data if the database is empty."""
    session = get_session()
    if session.query(Course).count() > 0:
        print("Data already exists.")
        session.close()
        return

    # Courses
    courses = [
        Course(name="Python Full Stack", duration_months=6, fee=35000),
        Course(name="Data Science", duration_months=4, fee=28000),
        Course(name="Java Full Stack", duration_months=6, fee=32000),
        Course(name="Web Development", duration_months=3, fee=18000),
    ]
    session.add_all(courses)
    session.flush()

    # Students
    students = [
        Student(name="Rahul Sharma", email="rahul@techpath.in", phone="9876543210", city="Bhopal"),
        Student(name="Priya Patel", email="priya@techpath.in", phone="9876543211", city="Pune"),
        Student(name="Amit Kumar", email="amit@techpath.in", phone="9876543212", city="Delhi"),
        Student(name="Sneha Gupta", email="sneha@techpath.in", phone="9876543213", city="Indore"),
        Student(name="Vikram Singh", email="vikram@techpath.in", phone="9876543214", city="Hyderabad"),
        Student(name="Ananya Reddy", email="ananya@techpath.in", phone="9876543215", city="Bhopal"),
    ]
    session.add_all(students)
    session.flush()

    # Enrollments
    enrollments = [
        Enrollment(student_id=1, course_id=1, status="active"),
        Enrollment(student_id=2, course_id=1, status="active"),
        Enrollment(student_id=3, course_id=3, status="active"),
        Enrollment(student_id=4, course_id=2, status="completed", grade="A"),
        Enrollment(student_id=5, course_id=1, status="active"),
        Enrollment(student_id=6, course_id=4, status="completed", grade="B"),
    ]
    session.add_all(enrollments)
    session.commit()
    print(f"Seeded: {len(courses)} courses, {len(students)} students, {len(enrollments)} enrollments")
    session.close()


def add_student():
    """Add a new student via user input."""
    session = get_session()
    name = input("Name: ").strip()
    if not name:
        print("Name cannot be empty.")
        session.close()
        return

    email = input("Email: ").strip()
    phone = input("Phone (10 digits): ").strip()
    city = input("City: ").strip() or "Bhopal"

    student = Student(name=name, email=email, phone=phone, city=city)
    session.add(student)
    try:
        session.commit()
        print(f"Added: {student.name} (ID: {student.id})")
    except Exception as e:
        session.rollback()
        print(f"Error: {e}")
    session.close()


def list_students():
    """Display all students in a table."""
    session = get_session()
    students = session.query(Student).order_by(Student.name).all()

    if not students:
        print("No students found.")
        session.close()
        return

    print(f"\n{'ID':<4} {'Name':<22} {'Email':<25} {'City':<12} {'Active'}")
    print("-" * 70)
    for s in students:
        active = "Yes" if s.is_active else "No"
        print(f"{s.id:<4} {s.name:<22} {s.email:<25} {s.city:<12} {active}")
    print(f"\nTotal: {len(students)} students")
    session.close()


def list_students_by_city():
    """Filter students by city."""
    session = get_session()
    city = input("Enter city: ").strip()
    students = session.query(Student).filter_by(city=city).all()

    if not students:
        print(f"No students from {city}.")
    else:
        print(f"\nStudents from {city}:")
        for s in students:
            print(f"  - {s.name} ({s.email})")
        print(f"Total: {len(students)}")
    session.close()


def list_courses():
    """Display all courses."""
    session = get_session()
    courses = session.query(Course).order_by(Course.fee.desc()).all()

    print(f"\n{'ID':<4} {'Course':<25} {'Months':<8} {'Fee':>10}")
    print("-" * 50)
    for c in courses:
        print(f"{c.id:<4} {c.name:<25} {c.duration_months:<8} Rs. {c.fee:>7,.0f}")
    session.close()


def show_enrollments():
    """Show each student's enrolled courses using relationship queries."""
    session = get_session()
    students = session.query(Student).options(
        joinedload(Student.enrollments).joinedload(Enrollment.course)
    ).all()

    for student in students:
        if student.enrollments:
            print(f"\n{student.name} ({student.city}):")
            for e in student.enrollments:
                grade = f" | Grade: {e.grade}" if e.grade else ""
                print(f"  -> {e.course.name} [{e.status}]{grade}")
        else:
            print(f"\n{student.name} ({student.city}): No enrollments")
    session.close()
```

Update `app.py` to test:
```python
from models import init_db
from crud import seed_data, list_students, list_courses, show_enrollments

def main():
    init_db()
    seed_data()
    list_courses()
    list_students()
    show_enrollments()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run `python app.py`.

**Verify:** You should see courses sorted by fee, all 6 students in a table, and each student's enrolled courses.

steps.title: Add Update and Delete Operations
steps.instructions:
Add these functions to `crud.py`:

```python
def update_student():
    """Update a student's details."""
    session = get_session()
    list_students()  # Show current students

    try:
        student_id = int(input("\nEnter Student ID to update: "))
    except ValueError:
        print("Invalid ID.")
        session.close()
        return

    student = session.query(Student).get(student_id)
    if not student:
        print("Student not found.")
        session.close()
        return

    print(f"\nUpdating: {student.name}")
    print("(Press Enter to keep current value)")

    name = input(f"Name [{student.name}]: ").strip()
    phone = input(f"Phone [{student.phone}]: ").strip()
    city = input(f"City [{student.city}]: ").strip()

    if name:
        student.name = name
    if phone:
        student.phone = phone
    if city:
        student.city = city

    session.commit()
    print(f"Updated: {student.name} ({student.city})")
    session.close()


def enroll_student():
    """Enroll a student in a course."""
    session = get_session()
    list_students()
    list_courses()

    try:
        student_id = int(input("\nStudent ID: "))
        course_id = int(input("Course ID: "))
    except ValueError:
        print("Invalid input.")
        session.close()
        return

    # Check if already enrolled
    existing = session.query(Enrollment).filter_by(
        student_id=student_id, course_id=course_id
    ).first()
    if existing:
        print("Student is already enrolled in this course.")
        session.close()
        return

    enrollment = Enrollment(student_id=student_id, course_id=course_id)
    session.add(enrollment)
    try:
        session.commit()
        student = session.query(Student).get(student_id)
        course = session.query(Course).get(course_id)
        print(f"Enrolled {student.name} in {course.name}")
    except Exception as e:
        session.rollback()
        print(f"Error: {e}")
    session.close()


def complete_enrollment():
    """Mark an enrollment as completed with a grade."""
    session = get_session()
    show_enrollments()

    try:
        student_id = int(input("\nStudent ID: "))
        course_id = int(input("Course ID: "))
    except ValueError:
        print("Invalid input.")
        session.close()
        return

    enrollment = session.query(Enrollment).filter_by(
        student_id=student_id, course_id=course_id
    ).first()

    if not enrollment:
        print("Enrollment not found.")
        session.close()
        return

    grade = input("Grade (A/B/C/D/F): ").strip().upper()
    enrollment.status = "completed"
    enrollment.grade = grade
    session.commit()
    print(f"Marked as completed with grade {grade}")
    session.close()


def delete_student():
    """Delete a student and their enrollments."""
    session = get_session()
    list_students()

    try:
        student_id = int(input("\nEnter Student ID to delete: "))
    except ValueError:
        print("Invalid ID.")
        session.close()
        return

    student = session.query(Student).get(student_id)
    if not student:
        print("Student not found.")
        session.close()
        return

    confirm = input(f"Delete {student.name}? This also removes their enrollments. (y/n): ").strip().lower()
    if confirm == "y":
        session.delete(student)
        session.commit()
        print(f"Deleted: {student.name}")
    else:
        print("Cancelled.")
    session.close()


def city_stats():
    """Show student count per city."""
    session = get_session()
    results = session.query(
        Student.city,
        func.count(Student.id).label("total")
    ).group_by(Student.city).order_by(func.count(Student.id).desc()).all()

    print("\nStudents per city:")
    print(f"{'City':<15} {'Count':>5}")
    print("-" * 22)
    for city, total in results:
        print(f"{city:<15} {total:>5}")
    session.close()
```

Test each function by calling them from `app.py` or directly.

**Verify:**
- `update_student()` changes a student's details and shows the updated value
- `enroll_student()` adds a new enrollment (rejects duplicates)
- `complete_enrollment()` updates status to "completed" with a grade
- `delete_student()` removes the student and their enrollments (cascade)
- `city_stats()` shows the count per city

steps.title: Build a Menu-Driven CLI Application
steps.instructions:
Replace the content of `app.py` with a full menu-driven interface:

```python
from models import init_db
from crud import (
    seed_data, add_student, list_students, list_students_by_city,
    list_courses, show_enrollments, update_student, enroll_student,
    complete_enrollment, delete_student, city_stats
)


def print_menu():
    print("\n" + "=" * 45)
    print("  TechPath Institute - Student Manager")
    print("=" * 45)
    print("  1.  List All Students")
    print("  2.  Add New Student")
    print("  3.  Update Student")
    print("  4.  Delete Student")
    print("  5.  Filter Students by City")
    print("  6.  City Statistics")
    print("  7.  List All Courses")
    print("  8.  Show Enrollments")
    print("  9.  Enroll Student in Course")
    print(" 10.  Complete Enrollment (Add Grade)")
    print("  0.  Exit")
    print("-" * 45)


def main():
    # Initialize database and seed data
    init_db()
    seed_data()

    while True:
        print_menu()
        choice = input("Choose an option: ").strip()

        if choice == "1":
            list_students()
        elif choice == "2":
            add_student()
        elif choice == "3":
            update_student()
        elif choice == "4":
            delete_student()
        elif choice == "5":
            list_students_by_city()
        elif choice == "6":
            city_stats()
        elif choice == "7":
            list_courses()
        elif choice == "8":
            show_enrollments()
        elif choice == "9":
            enroll_student()
        elif choice == "10":
            complete_enrollment()
        elif choice == "0":
            print("\nGoodbye from TechPath Institute!")
            break
        else:
            print("Invalid choice. Please try again.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run the application: `python app.py`

**Test these scenarios:**

| # | Action | Expected Result |
|---|--------|----------------|
| 1 | Choose 1 (List Students) | Table of 6 students with ID, Name, Email, City |
| 2 | Choose 7 (List Courses) | 4 courses sorted by fee descending |
| 3 | Choose 8 (Show Enrollments) | Each student's course with status |
| 4 | Choose 2 (Add Student) | Enter Neha Joshi, neha@techpath.in, Pune | New student appears in list |
| 5 | Choose 3 (Update Student) | Change Rahul's city to Hyderabad | Updated city shown |
| 6 | Choose 9 (Enroll Student) | Enroll new student in a course | Enrollment confirmed |
| 7 | Choose 10 (Complete) | Mark an enrollment as completed with grade A | Status updated |
| 8 | Choose 4 (Delete Student) | Delete a student | Student and enrollments removed |
| 9 | Choose 5 (Filter by City) | Enter "Bhopal" | Shows only Bhopal students |
| 10 | Choose 6 (City Stats) | Shows count per city | Correct numbers |
| 11 | Choose 0 (Exit) | Program ends cleanly |
